title: FreqBLiMP: Frequency-Controlled Minimal Pairs Reveal Robustness and Fragility of LLMs Under Lexical Rarity
abstract: arXiv:2609.07153v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Minimal-pair benchmarks such as BLiMP evaluate linguistic knowledge by testing whether language models (LMs) prefer acceptable sentences over minimally different unacceptable ones. However, these benchmarks largely ignore lexical frequency variation, despite lexical frequency being a pervasive and highly skewed property of natural language use. Consequently, existing evaluations do not test whether grammatical preferences remain stable when contrasts involve rare lexical items. We introduce FreqBLiMP, a frequency-controlled extension of BLiMP that regenerates all 67 paradigms under explicit Zipf-frequency regimes while preserving each minimal-pair's grammatical contrast. Evaluating multiple open-weight LLM families across scales, we find that decreasing lexical frequency produces a consistent, monotonic decrease in sentence likelihood, but only a modest reduction in overall contrastive acceptability accuracy. translated_title: FreqBLiMP：频率控制的最小对立对揭示大语言模型在词汇稀有性下的鲁棒性与脆弱性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2609.07153v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：诸如BLiMP等最小对立对基准通过测试语言模型是否偏好可接受的句子而非仅有微小差异的不可接受句子来评估其语言知识。然而，这些基准在很大程度上忽略了词汇频率的变化，尽管词汇频率是自然语言使用中普遍存在且高度偏斜的属性。因此，现有评估并未测试当对比涉及稀有词汇时，语法偏好是否仍能保持稳定。我们提出了FreqBLiMP，这是BLiMP的一个频率控制扩展，在明确的Zipf频率区间下重新生成了全部67个范式，同时保留了每个最小对立对的语法对比。通过对多个开源权重大语言模型家族在不同规模上进行评估，我们发现词汇频率的降低会导致句子似然的一致性单调下降，但对比可接受性判断准确率仅有适度降低。然而，这一总体上（摘要不完整，原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出FreqBLiMP——一个在明确Zipf频率区间下重新生成BLiMP全部67个语法范式的频率控制基准，发现词汇稀有性会一致且单调地降低大语言模型的句子似然，但其最小对立对的语法判断准确率仅受到适度影响。
en_tdlr: FreqBLiMP, a frequency-controlled extension of BLiMP regenerating all 67 paradigms under explicit Zipf-frequency regimes, reveals that lexical rarity consistently and monotonically degrades LLMs' sentence likelihoods while their minimal-pair grammatical accuracy remains only modestly affected.
